title: Refs KS-2021: a Pwned Passwords padding row (count 0) no longer makes a password count as breached
body:
## Refs KS-2021: a Pwned Passwords padding row (count 0) no longer makes a password count as breached

**TIER 1: product bytes change inside auth; tier 1 (Wednesday's ruling, model-routing rule 4: Spark edits inside auth, security, audit and hook files); the gate may raise it.** Two commits: round 1 (`2db221d43ad8`, one held Spark pass raised unchanged) and round 2 (`2eca13ad7e8c`, a fix round commissioned by Wednesday's ADDENDUM 1 after gate 331 read round 1 at `2db221d43ad8` as GO WITH NOTES). One product file changes, `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/password.ts` (+6 -2 against develop), with one new test file (+87). Merge to develop only.

Linear: https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-2021

## Summary

- **What changes.** `isPasswordBreached` asks the Pwned Passwords range endpoint for the password's 5-character hash prefix, then looks for the remaining suffix in the returned body. At develop it split each body line on `:` and compared only the suffix, so the count after the colon was ignored. The request sends `Add-Padding: true`, and a padding row carries count 0: it is not a breach record. A padding row that carried the user's own suffix therefore refused a clean password as breached. The loop reads `const [hashSuffix, countText] = line.trim().split(':');` and now returns true for `if (hashSuffix === suffix && countText?.trim() !== '0') return true;`. Round 1 (head `2db221d43ad8`) wrote `if (hashSuffix === suffix && Number(countText) > 0) return true;`. The function's other behaviour (the 2 second timeout, fail open on a non-200 answer or a thrown fetch, `HIBP_ENABLED=false`) is unchanged. Callers read in `services/auth/src` (not tests): register (`routes/auth.ts:214`), reset (`routes/auth.ts:898`) and change-password (`routes/users.ts:1009`).
- **Behaviour to read (round 2 replaces round 1's paragraph).** A body line for the user's own suffix is skipped ONLY when its count, trimmed, is exactly `0`. A malformed count for the user's own suffix (`S:` empty, `S` with no colon, `S:abc`, `S:-1`, `S:1,234`) REFUSES, as at develop, so no case flips from refuse to allow any more. Round 1's `Number(countText) > 0` let each of those through, silently (gate 331, G331-2209-1); gate 331 measured the fail-closed shape on its 25-shape corpus: it differs from develop only on rows whose count is exactly `0`. `S:00` still refuses; gate 331 read 0 leading-zero counts in the 2,006 lines of the one live range it fetched. The optional chain is deliberate (G331-2209-2): a row with no colon has no count, and a bare `countText.trim()` would throw, and the catch would allow the password.
- **The fetch-failure path is UNCHANGED by this PR.** A non-200 answer, a thrown fetch or the 2 second timeout still fails open (returns false), by Kam's ruling, exactly as at develop; each of those paths logs a warn line ("failing open") as before. This PR adds no log line and changes none.
- **The test.** `ks2021-hibp-range-match-needs-a-count-above-zero.test.ts` has 11 cells (the file name keeps round 1's words). Round 1: two red cells (R1: a padding row with count 0 carrying the password's suffix is not breached; R2: the same row in the middle of real rows) and three controls (C1: the suffix with count 3861493 is breached; C2: with the smallest real count, 1, is breached; C3: a body without the suffix is not breached). Round 2: R3, ONE table cell over five shapes of the own suffix (`''`, no colon, `abc`, `-1`, `1,234`), each expecting breached; and C4, a space before the suffix still matches (the line is trimmed first). The describe title and the header comment now say what holds. It drives the real module; the logger is a stand-in and the global `fetch` answers a plain body, so no network is used.
- **What it does NOT do.** It does not change the request, the timeout, the fail-open paths or the refusal text. It says `Refs`: whether KS-2021 is finished is the board seat's call after the merge.
- **Gate 331 findings.** G331-2209-1 (Minor): fixed in round 2. G331-2209-2 (Note): followed (optional chain with trim). G331-2209-3 (Note): the survivor `line.trim()` removed (M3) is now killed by C4 (measured below); `trimEnd` (M8) and the case-insensitive compare (M7) are not addressed and were not re-measured on the new line; `parseInt` (M6) was a mutant of round 1's line and does not exist in the new one. G331-2209-4 and -5 (Info): no change; the `seedDemoUsers` timer error did NOT appear in my one whole-suite run, and I make no claim about its rate. G331-2209-6 (Info): the literal `NO-PAIR` is below, and the "silent" wording above replaces round 1's.
- **Provenance.** Round 1 is the Spark operator's held pass (operator 133, 4,026 B canonical, sha256 prefix `09c98fbb953c06b0`), applied strictly at develop `581296f039b4` by Seat R 107th and raised unchanged. Round 2 is NOT a Spark patch: it is my own change to that PR, to the text of ADDENDUM 1.

## Test plan / Test Evidence

**Touched:** two files against develop `581296f039b4`: `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/services/password.ts` (6 added 2 removed) and `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks2021-hibp-range-match-needs-a-count-above-zero.test.ts` (new, 87 added); round 2 alone is +29 -4 over the same two files. The plan-time census (GraphQL, all pages, 102 open pull requests, 442 file rows) read no OTHER open pull request on either path; the controls passed (PR 2125's api-gateway file hit exactly PR 2125, the newest open PR's first file hit exactly that PR, an absent path hit nothing). The push gate re-ran the overlap and develop checks with this PR named in its ignore list. Develop moved twice while the push waited for the lock (PR 2203's squash `a6b62841d699`, two `services/transfer` files, then PR 2206's squash `cea1cdc2b07d`, one originate test file): the compare API reads 3 files in the move and none is one of this PR's two paths; the branch stays cut on `581296f039b4` and nothing was merged into it.

**Host and runtime (stated per the repo's test-discipline skill).** Every run below was made on one Apple Silicon Mac (arm64) with no Docker stack started (the cells use a stand-in logger and a stand-in `fetch`). Node is v26.8.1, the only Node on this machine; it is NOT the long-term-support line the repo's `CLAUDE.md` names (Node 24 today), nothing was run on Node 24, and the long-term-support status of Node 26 was not checked.

**Ran** (all by Seat R 108th, 2026-11-12, in tree `s-r107-ks2021` at commit `2eca13ad7e8c`; evidence `evidence/row2021r2/`):
- **Red first, then green.** With round 2's test kept and `password.ts` as at head `2db221d43ad8`: 5 failed (all R3, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`) and 6 passed (R1, R2, C1 to C4). After the change: the three HIBP-related files (ks2021, ks1968, ks1868-password-verify-hibp; 4 files) 47 of 47 passed.
- **Whole `services/auth` suite after the change:** 150 files, 1850 of 1850 passed, rc 0 (load1 6.35 at the start, 9.16 right after). Round 1's whole-suite numbers (149 files 1839 of 1839 on develop, 150 files 1844 of 1844 after round 1) were read by Seat R 107th and are not re-run; 1844 + 6 new cells = 1850.
- **Mutant M3 (`line.trim()` removed):** 1 failed of 11, and the failing cell is C4; the file was put back byte for byte (sha256 equal) and `git status` showed only my two files.
- **`tsc --noEmit`** on the service's own tsconfig: rc 0. **Test-type ratchet** (`scripts/typecheck-tests/check.cjs services/auth`): rc 0, "201 files, 150 under __tests__; 41 errors: 41 in the baseline, 0 new; 0 stale"; neither log names `password.ts` or the ks2021 test. **`eslint`** on the two files: rc 0, no output.
- **docs-fragments check** in the tree: rc 0, OK; it prints one ADVISORY about the committed cheat page differing from its render at line 6235, outside this PR's files. No fragment is added by this PR.
- **`npm run audit:gate`** in the tree: OK, 5 distinct advisories, 5 baselined.

**NOT run:** the real Pwned Passwords service (no network: the cells answer a plain body); the register, reset and change-password routes end to end; the real auth service against a database or the Docker stack; mutants M7 and M8 on the new line; the other packages' suites; the four platform suites (Schemathesis, Akto, Playwright, k6); any CI run (retired for this repo). The pre-push hook's legs (below) run the repo's checks on the pushed head.

**Docs fragments and changed-line comments (the repo's test-discipline skill).** Section 4 of the skill asks for a flow and a cheat-sheet fragment pair with every test change. This PR raises a held local-model patch under the coordinating seat's **NO-PAIR** ruling, and round 2 follows it, so this PR adds no pair. Every changed line of round 2 carries a why-and-ticket comment (`password.ts`, the test header, the describe title, R3 and C4). The gap is recorded for a follow-up across the held-patch pull requests of this lane.

**Migrations + config:** none.

**Pre-push hook:** (quoted from the push of this head by Seat R 108th)
```
PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.
  legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it.
  This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.
```
The push (956 s, rc 0) moved the branch `2db221d43..2eca13ad7` as a fast-forward; `ls-remote` read the branch and `refs/pull/2209/head` at `2eca13ad7e8c`. The legs that ran include leg 6 (the audit gate), leg 14 (the shell suites of a TS-only push) and leg 16 (the test-type ratchet: auth 41 baselined, 0 new); legs 3, 4 and 8 did not run, so this is not a full pre-push pass.

## Before this deploys

- Nothing deploys from this PR. It reaches develop only; "deployed" reads as "on develop". The auth service image would need a rebuild for the change to run anywhere, and the demo is frozen: none is granted by this PR.

## Notes for the gate

- **Round 2 only** needs a re-read: one product line (`password.ts` line 178's condition, plus its comment lines) and two test additions (R3, C4) with the describe title and header comment. Round 1's patch is untouched.
- Branch name `feature/ks-2021-auth-hibp-check-the-range-body-match` is Linear's own suggestion for the ticket; it carries no other ticket's key and no closing word.
